proof_attempt_summary: Discovery proposed a fixed-tuple matched marginal-counterfactual Wasserstein minimax theorem using mixed-rank corrections. One scoped revision removed inherited lower and oracle results from the root targets, but the final reviewer and independent adjudication still found the sole root question identical to the parent frontier. No D0 derivation or Lean formalization ran; the analytic attainer draft remains unverified, and any new experiment or estimand requires a fresh topic.
tldr: The sharp expected marginal \(W_1\) risk on the fixed six-dimensional sectional class \(\mathcal M\) requires an explicit matched rate \(r_n\), every unavoidable logarithm, a total observable probability-valued attainer and a same-class all-estimator converse. Unknown \(e\) interacts with covariate-varying \(\eta\) across a growing outcome dictionary; scale-dependent covariate corrections can require ranks greater than \(n\). The banked \(\ell_n=n^{-243/697}\) lower baseline and the Niles-Weed--Berthet randomized \(n^{-5/14}\) benchmark are credited background. DoubleGen shares the identified causal marginal, but its loss guarantees and additional rate hypotheses do not settle this experiment. The matched-risk theorem is the sole research deliverable.
gap: The parent has an interaction lower baseline and probability reconstruction but no matching observable high-rank coefficient certificate. Direct-density coefficients contain no estimated inverse propensity; scalar corrected-functional theory does not supply the outcome-scale-dependent sectional approximation and simultaneous transport aggregation for a growing dictionary.
fill: The sole root question derives the matched risk, a total probability attainer and the same-class converse. Its estimator handle combines scale-dependent higher corrections with signed transport aggregation and finite probability reconstruction. The background generator comparison distinguishes inclusion in the public identified model from satisfaction of its procedure-specific rate conditions. DoubleGen and DecFM are consumers of the resulting benchmark; their empirical populations are not asserted to lie in \(\mathcal M\).
